extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons / ASSIST users and institutional grant administrators (SOs/AOs/PIs/AA/ASST) preparing and managing NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and rules for account association, password management, assigning/modifying/revoking user access and privileges, attachment handling, and access-history auditing within the NIH ASSIST application submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct eRA Commons URL
rubrics_metrics.description: Also, ensure that you not are not using old bookmarked URLs to access eRA Commons. The URL for eRA Commons is https://public.era.nih.gov/commons/.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the current public.era.nih.gov/commons URL rather than old bookmarks to avoid login/association problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: InCommon Federation and two-factor authentication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you have an active account with an organization that participates with the InCommon Federation and you know your password. Your organization must support NIH’s two-factor authentication standards and you must have two-factor authentication enabled for your account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot associate or sign in with your organization's credentials unless the organization participates in InCommon and supports NIH 2‑factor authentication; ensure 2FA is enabled on your organizational account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account association step (enter eRA credentials)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Associate Your eRA Account screen, enter your eRA Commons User ID and password. Click the Continue button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If successful, your eRA account will be associated with your organization's account and you will be logged in without needing your eRA username/password again. This is a one-time association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot use system-assigned temporary password to associate accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have not yet created your own eRA account password and are attempting to associate your accounts using the system-assigned, temporary password for your eRA account, you will receive an error. You must change your eRA account password to one of your choosing before you can associate your accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log into Commons with the temporary password, change it to a personal password, then retry association using the new password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expired password blocks association
rubrics_metrics.description: You will not be able to associate your accounts if your eRA account password is expired. Navigate to the Commons home page. Use the Commons Login fields to log into Commons with your expired password. Commons will present the Change Password screen on which you can update your password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change expired password at Commons first (see Reset Your Expired Password), then proceed to associate accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locked account reset via Forgot Password/Unlock Account
rubrics_metrics.description: You can reset your eRA account by clicking the Forgot Password/Unlock Account link on eRA Commons home page. Commons will generate a new, temporary password for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the password reset flow to obtain a temporary password, then change it to a password of your choosing before attempting association or login.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passwords must follow NIH eRA Password Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When changing your password, remember that all passwords must follow the NIH eRA Password Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the NIH eRA Password Policy for complexity, length, expiration and other constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgot Password/Unlock Account submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: From the ASSIST login page, click the Forgot Password/Unlock Account link. The Reset Password screen displays. Enter your User ID (this is the same as your User Name) and Email address into the displayed fields. Both fields are required. The email address must match that of your personal profile in Commons. Select the Submit button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system returns to the ASSIST login page and emails a new temporary password to the email on file; use it to log in and then change your password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access control variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Application access can be controlled across three variables: 1) Edit vs. View, 2) Entire application vs. specific component within an application (for multi-project applications), 3) Budget data vs. Non-Budget data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign access levels with these three dimensions in mind to tailor who can view or edit which parts of the application and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic privileges based on eRA Commons role — Signing Official (SO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing Official (SO) at the lead application organization: Initiate application; Assign, modify, or revoke application access for other users; Delegate ability to assign, modify, or revoke application access for other users; Edit entire application; Submit application (must be SO at lead applicant organization AND have valid Grants.gov Authorized Organization Representative credentials); Update the component status from WIP to Final (without setting it to Complete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These privileges are automatically available and cannot be individually granted/revoked via Manage Access in ASSIST.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic privileges based on eRA Commons role — Administrative Official (AO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Official (AO) at the lead applicant organization: Initiate application; Edit entire application; Update the component status from WIP to Final (without setting it to Complete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AO automatic privileges are tied to the role and organization and are not individually managed in ASSIST.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic privileges based on eRA Commons role — Principal Investigator (PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigator (PI) identified on an application: Edit entire application; Delegate access to another PI on their behalf enabling delegated PI to initiate and work on HSS request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs have broad edit capabilities and limited delegation rights as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported delegation types and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegations from Commons that are supported within ASSIST: Progress Report (SO, AA, AO delegated by -> PI) enables the second PI to initiate and submit a progress report or initiate and submit an HSS request for the first PI; Progress Report (PI delegated -> any active user within the Organization) enables the authorized user to initiate and edit an RPPR or HSS request; Submit (SO, BO delegated -> PI) enables the PI to submit (progress report or HSS Request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the delegation mapping: who delegates to whom and what actions the delegate is enabled to perform (RPPR, HSS, submit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Component-level automatic privileges when UEI/DUNS entered
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of multi-project applications, once the DUNS or UEI (Unique Entity Identifier) number is entered on the SF424 R&R for a component, then similar automatic privileges apply for that specific component. You cannot revoke the automatic access given to the SOs of the component through Manage Access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a component is in any status other than Work In Progress, the component can only be edited by individuals granted edit access to the entire application; component-level automatic access alone is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add user — required information and access options
rubrics_metrics.description: To add a new user, enter the eRA Commons ID into the Username field. Select appropriate access for the Overall Component and/or additional components or the Entire Application by selecting one of the options - None, Edit, or View - from the Budget, Non-Budget, and All drop-down lists. If assigning different access for Budget and Non-Budget, use the individual lists; if same access, use All.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple attachments or components, set access per component as needed; choose All to set Budget and Non-Budget simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access Maintainer granting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an SO/AOR with the Applicant Lead Organization can grant or revoke the Entire Application Access Maintainer access level. This can only be granted to a PI or ASST associated with the institution of the SO/AOR. Any user holding the Entire Application Access Maintainer access level has the ability to grant Entire Application Access levels – other than the Entire Application Access Maintainer level – to any AA, AO, ASST, PI, or SO. Only an SO/AOR with the Component Lead Organization can grant or revoke the Component Access Maintainer level. This can only be granted to a PI or ASST associated with the institution of the SO/AOR. Any user holding the Component Access Maintainer access level has the ability to grant any Component Access levels – other than Component Access Maintainer – to any AA, AO, AST, PI, or SO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access Maintainer is a powerful privilege with strict grantor constraints (SO/AOR) and can be delegated only to specific roles associated with the same institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire Application Status Maintainer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an SO or AO from the Applicant Lead Organization can grant or revoke the Status Maintainer access level. By default, the Initiator of the application is given access to this level. Status Maintainer level includes the ability to update the status of an individual component (Complete, Final, Abandoned, WIP) as well as the status of the entire application (All Components Final, Abandoned, Ready for Submission). The Status Maintainer privilege for an entire application cannot be granted to an individual who does not hold the entire application Edit privilege as well (i.e., All column, option Edit). The checkbox for the Status Maintainer privilege is disabled until the Edit privilege is added for that individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant Status Maintainer only to users who also have Edit privileges for the entire application; Initiator gets this by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASSIST email notifications for access changes
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST automatically sends an email notification to the user assigned the access. The email notification informs the user of the access levels given, to which application or components of that application the access applies, and the user who granted the access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users will be notified automatically on add/modify/revoke actions; expect emails to include who granted the access and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify user access workflow and same privilege rules apply
rubrics_metrics.description: To modify access, select the user from the User Access Summary and make appropriate changes by selecting None, Edit, or View from the Budget, Non-Budget, and All drop-down lists. Optional: select Access Maintainer or Status Maintainer checkboxes (subject to the same governance rules as when granting access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifying access triggers automatic email notifications informing of changes, including who made the changes and which application/components are affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to revoke access
rubrics_metrics.description: To revoke specific access: update the Budget, Non-Budget, and/or All access by selecting None and click Save. To revoke access maintainer: unselect the Access Maintainer checkbox and click Save. To revoke status maintainer: unselect the Status Maintainer checkbox and click Save. To revoke all set access levels: select the Revoke All Accesses button and confirm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revoking an individual's entire application Edit privilege also removes their Status Maintainer privilege (where applicable). Users whose access has been revoked receive email notifications including the application, the person who revoked the access, and the access level revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain institution-based privileges are irrevocable via ASSIST
rubrics_metrics.description: Some access levels cannot be revoked. The institution-based privileges automatically granted to SOs and AOs cannot be revoked. The PD/PIs for the application must have at least Entire Application Viewer access level, and the Project Lead must have at least the Component (All) Viewer access level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan around the fact that SO/AO institutional privileges persist and minimal viewer access is enforced for PD/PIs and Project Leads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage Access History contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The access history provides details about the access granted or revoked for an application and its components. This detail includes such information as the username and organization, the action taken against the account, the access level granted, the component to which access was granted, username of the person who granted the access, and the date on which the action occurred. The Manage Access History page includes: User; Primary Organization; Action taken (e.g., access granted or access revoked); Access Level; Component ID: Title; Update User; Date of Event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Manage Access History to audit who was granted or revoked which access and when, for each user/component combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: User Access History per-user view
rubrics_metrics.description: The User Access History page displays for the selected user. Information regarding this user's access is included for the Overall Application and all additional components, regardless of which was selected from the User Access Summary. The information includes: User; Primary Organization; Action taken (e.g., access granted or access revoked); Access Level; Component ID: Title; Update User; Date of Event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a user from User Access Summary then View User Access History to see their full access timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions list and availability rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Actions section lists potential buttons for an ASSIST user. The buttons available to an individual ASSIST user vary depending on such conditions as the privileges granted to the user, the stage in the work flow, the status of the application, whether a single- or multi-project application, the part of the application being worked on, etc. The topic lists potential Actions buttons (e.g., Add New Component; Add Optional Form; Change Component Order; Copy Application; Delete Application; Delete Component; Display Component Status; Manage Access; Preview Application; Preview Current Component; Preview Current Form; Restore Previous Version; Return to Application Information; Submit Application; Update Component Status; Update Submission Status; Validate Application; Validate Component; View Status History (for the application); View Status History (for a component of a multi-project application)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the set of actionable buttons to change with role, status, and application type; consult this list to know possible actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Some form fields allow or call for attachments, which must be in the form of a PDF. Please review the NIH eRA guidelines for formatting attachments before attaching documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All attachments must be PDF and comply with NIH formatting guidance (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file-name uniqueness rule
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPORTANT: You must use unique file names for multiple attachments within the same form. Duplicate file names can exist across multiple forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding multiple attachments to a single form field, ensure each file name is unique to avoid conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add Attachment workflow and single vs multiple behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: To add an attachment: From any area on a form with an attachment field, click the Add Attachment button. A popup opens to search for the file. Use the Browse button within the popup to search for the PDF file. With the file selected, click the Submit button. For fields allowing a single attachment, the Add Attachment button on the form field is replaced by the Replace Attachment, Delete Attachment, and View Attachment buttons. The attached file name displays within the field. Fields allowing multiple attachments display the files in a table. Update and View buttons display for each attached file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Add/Replace/Delete semantics appropriate to whether the form field allows single or multiple attachments; filenames and file format rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace Attachment workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: To replace an attachment from a field allowing only one attachment: select the Replace Attachment button, use the Browse button in the popup to search for the PDF file, select it, and click Submit. For fields allowing multiple attachments: select the Update button in the Update Attachment column for the specific file, then browse and submit the new file. The form/table updates with the replaced file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Replace/Update controls depending on single/multiple-attachment fields; replaced files display immediately in the field or table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delete Attachment workflow (single vs multiple)
rubrics_metrics.description: File attachments display differently depending on whether the field allows one attachment or multiple attachments. To delete an attachment from a field allowing only one attachment: From any form field with an attachment, select the Delete Attachment button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fields allowing multiple attachments, use the table's controls to delete the specific file; follow on-screen prompts to confirm deletion.
